1 # 37_worktrunk.zsh - Worktrunk (`wt`) git worktree manager
2 # https://worktrunk.dev — github.com/max-sixty/worktrunk
3 #
4 # Companion config: ~/.config/worktrunk/config.toml (managed by chezmoi at
5 # dot_config/worktrunk/config.toml). Aliases like `wt sw` / `wt cc` live
6 # THERE, not here — keep this file focused on shell-level integration only.
7 
8 # Skip silently if not installed (Linux ansible install can fail offline)
9 command -v wt &>/dev/null || return 0
10 
11 # ── Shell integration: cd-wrapping `wt` function ───────────────────────────
12 #
13 # `wt switch` needs to change the parent shell's $PWD, which a normal binary
14 # can't do. Worktrunk solves this by writing a directive file that a wrapper
15 # shell function reads and `cd`s to. We eval that wrapper at shell startup
16 # rather than running `wt config shell install` (which edits ~/.zshrc with a
17 # block chezmoi would fight over).
18 #
19 # Same pattern as starship / zoxide / direnv elsewhere in this directory.
20 eval "$(wt config shell init zsh 2>/dev/null)"
21 
22 # ── Completion ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
23 #
24 # macOS (Homebrew): `_wt` ships in /opt/homebrew/share/zsh/site-functions/
25 # and is picked up automatically by compinit — nothing to do here.
26 #
27 # Linux (ansible drops the bare binary into ~/.local/bin/) has no system
28 # completion path, so dump clap's auto-generated zsh completer into
29 # ~/.zfunc/_wt (already on $fpath via dot_zshrc.tmpl). Same pattern as sesh /
30 # television. Regenerate when wt's version changes.
31 #
32 # Worktrunk doesn't expose a `wt completion zsh` subcommand — clap's dynamic
33 # completer is invoked via `COMPLETE=zsh wt` (with no args). Output is a
34 # self-contained `#compdef wt` script that handles further completion
35 # requests by re-invoking the binary with COMPLETE+_CLAP_COMPLETE_INDEX set.
36 if [[ -d ~/.zfunc ]] && [[ ! -f /opt/homebrew/share/zsh/site-functions/_wt ]] \
37                     && [[ ! -f /usr/local/share/zsh/site-functions/_wt ]]; then
38     local _wt_ver="$(wt --version 2>/dev/null)"
39     if [[ ! -f ~/.zfunc/_wt ]] || ! grep -q "${_wt_ver}" ~/.zfunc/_wt 2>/dev/null; then
40         {
```

1 # 38_workmux.zsh - Workmux (`workmux` / `wm`) tmux + git-worktree orchestrator
2 # https://workmux.raine.dev — github.com/raine/workmux

4 # Companion config: ~/.config/workmux/config.yaml (managed by chezmoi at
5 # dot_config/workmux/config.yaml). See docs/tools/workmux.md for the full
6 # story (worktrunk vs workmux split, status icon lifecycle, leak mitigation).
7 #
8 # Why a separate file from 37_worktrunk.zsh: the two tools coexist (worktrunk
9 # = `wt` for git-worktree CLI / aliases, workmux = `wm` for status icons +
10 # dashboard + sidebar). Separate files keep the rationale + helpers per-tool
11 # and let users disable one independently.
12 
13 # Skip silently if not installed (Linux ansible install can fail offline,
14 # Cargo path may not be present, etc.)
15 command -v workmux &>/dev/null || return 0
16 
17 # ── Manual marker cleanup ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
18 #
19 # The `working` (🤖) status workmux sets is *sticky* — it never auto-clears
20 # on its own. `waiting` (💬) and `done` (✅) auto-clear when you focus the
21 # window, but `working` only goes away when:
22 #   1. The agent's plugin/hook explicitly calls `workmux set-window-status done`
23 #      (Claude Stop / OpenCode session.idle), OR
24 #   2. `workmux sidebar` is running and detects 10s of pane silence
25 #      (interrupted-agent detection), OR
26 #   3. You manually clear it.
27 #
28 # Path #1 fails when the agent is killed before its Stop/idle handler fires
29 # (Ctrl+C, terminal crash, OOM). Path #2 requires keeping a sidebar pane open.
30 # `wmclear` is the manual escape hatch.
31 #
32 # Without arg: clears the marker for the current tmux window.
33 # With arg:    `wmclear 5` clears window 5 in the current session.
34 # Pass `--all` to nuke every workmux marker in the current session.
35 function wmclear() {
36     if [[ "$1" == "--all" ]]; then
37         # Walk every window in the current session and unset the user-var
38         local sess
39         sess=$(tmux display -p '#{session_name}' 2>/dev/null) || return 1
40         local -a windows
```

1 # ~/.config/shell/60_tmux_status.sh
2 # Source: dot_config/shell/60_tmux_status.sh (managed by chezmoi)
3 #
4 # Generic per-window tmux status badge helpers — POSIX, sourced by both
5 # zsh and bash. Thin convenience layer over the same primitive workmux
6 # uses (`tmux set-option -w '@<name>_status' '<glyph>'`), so any script /
7 # hook / cron job / build watcher can tag its tmux window without
8 # pulling in workmux.
9 #
10 # Why a shared layer (not in 38_workmux.zsh): these helpers don't need
11 # any zsh feature, and the most common consumers (build scripts, deploy
12 # hooks, CI wrappers) tend to be `#!/bin/bash` or `#!/bin/sh`. Putting
13 # them in dot_config/shell/ means they Just Work from any shell.
14 #
15 # Companion: docs/tools/workmux.md → "Reusing the per-window status
16 # mechanism (without workmux)" for design rationale, the lifecycle hard
17 # rules, and the build-watcher worked example.
18 #
19 # Quick reference:
20 #
21 #   tmux_status_set my_build 🔨           # tag current window
22 #   tmux_status_set my_build 🔨 mysess:3  # tag specific window
23 #   tmux_status_get my_build              # read current window
24 #   tmux_status_clear my_build            # unset (current window)
25 #   tmux_status_clear my_build mysess:3   # unset specific window
26 #   tmux_status_clear_all my_build        # unset across every session
27 #   tmux_status_list                      # list every @*_status user-var
28 #   tmux_status_run my_build 🔨 ✅ ❌ -- npm run build
29 #                                         # set 🔨, run cmd, set ✅/❌
30 #                                         # by exit code, auto-clear on
31 #                                         # signal trap
32 #
33 # Naming convention: pass the LOGICAL name without `@` or `_status`
34 # suffix — these helpers add the `@<name>_status` wrapper. So
35 # `tmux_status_set my_build 🔨` writes `@my_build_status`. This keeps
36 # the user-var namespace tidy (`@<tool>_status` everywhere) and lets
37 # you grep for "every status producer" with `tmux_status_list`.
38 
39 # Skip silently if tmux isn't on PATH (cron, headless SSH, fresh box
40 # pre-ansible). Producers can call these unconditionally.
```

```text
1 #!/usr/bin/env bash
2 # Top-level tmux popup menu — invoked by `prefix + Space`.
3 #
4 # Why a script (not inline `display-menu` in keybindings.conf):
5 #   1. tmux's command parser stops at literal `;`, `{`, `}` even inside
6 #      nested quotes. With ~50 menu rows full of fzf binds and shell
7 #      one-liners, escaping became fragile and broke silently.
8 #   2. tmux `display-menu` does not paginate. If the menu is taller than
9 #      the terminal, the entire popup is suppressed with no error. By
10 #      generating the menu here we can read $TMUX client_height and
11 #      auto-trim low-frequency rows when small.
12 #   3. Submenus are normal `tmux display-menu` invocations from rows;
13 #      they don't share quoting context with the parent menu.
14 #
15 # Submenus live in sibling scripts:
16 #   menu-layouts.sh, menu-session.sh, menu-sesh.sh,
17 #   menu-popups.sh, menu-theme.sh, menu-system.sh, menu-agents.sh
18 #
19 # See: pitfalls/tmux-display-menu-silent-parse-failure.md
20 
21 set -euo pipefail
22 
23 H=$(tmux display-message -p '#{client_height}')
24 DIR=~/.config/tmux
25 
26 # Tier 0: ALWAYS shown (highest frequency, ~7 rows + 2 separators)
27 declare -a tier0=(
28   "Last window"  Tab "last-window"
29   "Last pane"    P   "last-pane"
30   ""             ""  ""
31   "Choose win"   w   "choose-tree -Zw"
32   "Choose sess"  s   "choose-tree -Zs"
33   "Pane #s"      q   "display-panes -d 0"
34   ""             ""  ""
35   "Sesh picker"  g   "run-shell '$DIR/sesh-picker.sh'"
36   "Lazygit"      G   "display-popup -E -w 90% -h 90% -d '#{pane_current_path}' -T ' lazygit ' 'lazygit'"
37 )
38 
39 # Tier 1: shown when height >= 22 (adds new-window/split/zoom)
40 declare -a tier1=(
41   ""             ""  ""
42   "New window"   c   "new-window -c '#{pane_current_path}'"
43   "Split |"      "|" "split-window -h -c '#{pane_current_path}'"
44   "Split -"      "-" "split-window -v -c '#{pane_current_path}'"
45   "Zoom"         z   "resize-pane -Z"
46 )
47 
48 # Tier 2: submenus + cheatsheet (always shown if Tier 1 is shown)
49 declare -a tier2=(
50   ""             ""  ""
```

```text
1 # tmux + OSC 133 capture helpers — shell-level counterparts of the
2 # prefix + M-y / M-i tmux bindings, with an N-back index.
3 #
4 #   cpcmd [N]    last (or Nth-latest) command's INPUT  (zsh history; universal)
5 #   cpout [N]    last (or Nth-latest) command's OUTPUT (tmux copy-mode chain)
6 #   cpblock [N]  last (or Nth-latest) command's FULL BLOCK, Warp-style
7 #
8 # N defaults to 1 (= latest). N=2 is the one before that, and so on.
9 #
10 # Each prints captured text to stdout (pipe-friendly: `cpout | grep ERROR`)
11 # AND copies to system clipboard. Diagnostic + byte count go to stderr so
12 # stdout stays clean for pipes.
13 #
14 # WHY cpout/cpblock need tmux:
15 # tmux consumes OSC 133 marker bytes and only stores them as per-line
16 # attributes in its grid — `tmux capture-pane -pe` does NOT re-emit them.
17 # Outside tmux there's no portable way to recover boundaries of a past
18 # command's output (terminals like iTerm2/Ghostty have proprietary APIs,
19 # but nothing cross-terminal). cpcmd uses zsh shell history instead, so it
20 # works universally.
21 #
22 # Requires: zsh; plus tmux for cpout/cpblock.
23 
24 # Pipe stdin to system clipboard, preferring tmux's OSC 52 bridge (SSH-safe)
25 # and falling back to platform-native clipboard tools.
26 _cpx_to_clipboard() {
27   if [[ -n "$TMUX" ]]; then
28     tmux load-buffer -w -
29   elif command -v pbcopy &>/dev/null; then
30     pbcopy
31   elif command -v wl-copy &>/dev/null; then
32     wl-copy
33   elif command -v xclip &>/dev/null; then
34     xclip -selection clipboard -in
35   elif command -v xsel &>/dev/null; then
36     xsel --clipboard --input
37   else
38     cat >/dev/null
39     return 1
40   fi
41 }
42 
43 # Validate a positive-integer argument. Echoes the value on success; prints
44 # a usage hint to stderr and returns 1 on invalid input.
45 _cpx_parse_n() {
46   local name=$1 n=${2:-1}
47   if [[ ! "$n" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || (( n < 1 )); then
48     print -u2 "$name: N must be a positive integer (got: $n). Usage: $name [N]"
49     return 1
50   fi
```

1 #!/usr/bin/env bash
2 # Coding-agent submenu — discovery + management of live agent sessions.
3 #
4 # Reached from the top popup menu (prefix + Space → → Agents). The two `tv`
5 # entries are the primary surfaces; recon is offered only when installed.
6 #
7 # See: docs/tools/agent-panes-discovery.md
8 set -euo pipefail
9 
10 declare -a rows=(
11   "Live agent panes (tv)"     a "display-popup -E -w 80% -h 70% -d '#{pane_current_path}' -T ' Live agent panes ' 'tv agent-panes'"
12   "Stored sessions (tv)"      s "display-popup -E -w 80% -h 70% -d '#{pane_current_path}' -T ' Agent sessions ' 'tv agent-sessions'"
13 )
14 
15 # recon is Claude-only and optional (cargo install). Probe before adding the
16 # row so the menu doesn't show a dead entry on hosts that haven't installed it.
17 if command -v recon >/dev/null 2>&1; then
18   rows+=(

# --- claude-plans-here -----------------------------------------------------
# Scaffold or update project-local .claude/settings.json so Claude Code's
# /plan files land in ./.claude/plans/ (kept inside the repo) instead of the
# user-global plansDirectory. Pairs well with the agent-history-hygiene skill,
# which can then redact + commit the plan files alongside the diff.
#
# Also offers to import "orphan" plans — plans previously written under the
# global ~/.claude/plans/ that belong to this project. Detection: scan
# ~/.claude/projects/<encoded-cwd>/*.jsonl (where Claude Code logs sessions
# per cwd; encoding maps '/' and '.' to '-') for Write/Edit tool_use entries
# whose file_path points into ~/.claude/plans/. This avoids false positives
# from sessions that merely *mentioned* a plan path in conversation.
#
# Usage: claude-plans-here [-f] [-y]
#   -f   auto-yes the settings.json merge prompt
#   -y   auto-yes the orphan-plan copy prompt
claude-plans-here() {
 force_settings=0
 force_orphans=0
 while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
  case "$1" in
  -f) force_settings=1 ;;
  -y) force_orphans=1 ;;
  -h | --help)
   echo "Usage: claude-plans-here [-f] [-y]"
   echo "  -f   auto-yes the settings.json merge prompt"
   echo "  -y   auto-yes the orphan-plan copy prompt"
   return 0
   ;;
  *)
   echo "claude-plans-here: unknown flag '$1'" >&2
   return 1
   ;;
  esac
  shift
 done

 target=".claude/settings.json"
 mkdir -p .claude/plans

 if [ ! -e "$target" ]; then
  cat >"$target" <<'EOF'
{
  "plansDirectory": "./.claude/plans"
}
EOF
  echo "Wrote $PWD/$target"
 else

### Workmux status icon integration spans 6 files

Touching the `🤖`/`💬`/`✅` per-tmux-window status mechanism requires keeping these 6 surfaces in sync (full story: [docs/tools/workmux.md](docs/tools/workmux.md); pitfall: [pitfalls/workmux-status-leak.md](pitfalls/workmux-status-leak.md)):

1. `dot_ansible/roles/devtools/tasks/main.yml` — binary install (brew tap on macOS; GitHub release `.tar.gz` on Linux)
2. `dot_config/workmux/config.yaml` — `status_format: false` is load-bearing
3. `dot_config/tmux/theme.catppuccin.conf` — `#{?@workmux_status, #{@workmux_status},}` appended to `@catppuccin_window_text` and `@catppuccin_window_current_text`
4. `dot_claude/modify_settings.json` — `Stop`/`SubagentStop`/`UserPromptSubmit`/`Notification` hooks calling `workmux set-window-status` (hook-aware merger preserves CodeIsland entries)
5. `dot_config/opencode/plugins/workmux-status.ts` + `dot_config/opencode/modify_package.json`
6. `dot_config/shell/60_tmux_status.sh` — generic POSIX `tmux_status_set/get/clear/clear_all/list/run` for non-agent producers

**Hard rules**: never run `workmux setup` on a managed machine (would write parallel hook entries); never flip `status_format: true` (fights catppuccin's window-text override); never drop the `command -v workmux >/dev/null 2>&1 && … || true` guard in Claude hooks (spams errors on fresh boxes); never drop explicit `set-window-status done` from `Stop`/`SubagentStop` (upstream only ever sets `working`, never clears — that's the by-design leak documented in the pitfall). `wt` (worktrunk, `37_worktrunk.zsh`) and `wm` (workmux, `38_workmux.zsh`) stay distinct — different config formats, killer features, helper files.

## Chezmoi templating conventions

**Hard rule**: before adding `{{ if eq .profile … }}`, ask if the predicate is auto-detectable. If yes, use `.chezmoi.os` / `.chezmoi.arch` / `.chezmoi.hostname`. `.profile` is for user-role choices only. Values are limited to `macos`, `ubuntu_desktop`, `ubuntu_server` — do **not** introduce new values for OS/arch facts (historical `macos_intel` profile was removed for exactly this reason).

| Predicate | Use |
|---|---|
--
- Do **not** broaden the gate to `bindkey -M viins`/`vicmd` calls inside `dot_config/zsh/tools/*.zsh` — harmless no-ops without zsh-vi-mode loaded.
- The `minimal` bundle in `scripts/init/dotfiles_init.py` forces `enableVimMode = False` (CI/Docker). Don't change without explicit user request.
- New vim-touched file → follow the "Yes, gate it" / "No, leave it alone" flow in `docs/this_repo/vim-mode.md` → "For maintainers", and add it to the catalog table in that same page.

### Install vs upgrade is split on purpose

`chezmoi apply` + ansible is **install-only** (`state: present`, `creates:`). Explicit upgrade path: [`scripts/upgrade_tools.sh`](scripts/upgrade_tools.sh) via `just upgrade-*`. `scripts/**` is in `.chezmoiignore.tmpl`, so the upgrade script runs from the repo, never deployed.

**Hard rules**:

- Do **not** rewrite ansible roles to `state: latest`.
- Do **not** add `apt upgrade` / system package bumps to default scope.
- **Minimum-version exception**: a role MAY auto-upgrade a single tool inside `chezmoi apply` when it legitimately needs a newer version (e.g. `python_uv_tools` needs `uv >= 0.8.5` for `--with-executables-from`). MUST detect install style (brew vs curl/standalone) and dispatch — never blindly `uv self update` (no-op on brew uv) or `brew upgrade uv` (errors if not a brew formula). Dispatch helper is mirrored in `scripts/upgrade_tools.sh::cat_uv()` and `dot_ansible/roles/python_uv_tools/tasks/main.yml`. See [docs/this_repo/uv-bootstrap.md](docs/this_repo/uv-bootstrap.md), [pitfalls/uv-self-update-homebrew-noop.md](pitfalls/uv-self-update-homebrew-noop.md), [pitfalls/ansible-when-regex-replace-backslash-strip.md](pitfalls/ansible-when-regex-replace-backslash-strip.md).
- **`with_executables_from:` entries MUST also declare `extra_binaries:`** in `dot_ansible/roles/python_uv_tools/defaults/main.yml`. Without it the install guard short-circuits on hosts where the primary binary already exists, and entry-point shims are never written (silent missing `jupyter` / `jupyter-notebook` despite `jupyter-lab` present). Audit: `yq '.python_uv_tools[] | select(.with_executables_from) | select(.extra_binaries == null) | .name' …` MUST print nothing. See [pitfalls/uv-tool-install-creates-guard-misses-executables-from.md](pitfalls/uv-tool-install-creates-guard-misses-executables-from.md).
- New upgrade category: [docs/this_repo/upgrades.md → Adding a new category](docs/this_repo/upgrades.md). For a tool already managed by brew/uv/npm/cargo/dotnet/gem/mise: do nothing — generic `upgrade` picks it up.

### Sudo session is shared across all run-scripts

All three `run_*` scripts share one sudo session via `scripts/lib/sudo_shared.sh` — user prompted once at `chezmoi apply` start, reused silently downstream.

**Hard rules**:

3 #
4 # Generic per-window tmux status badge helpers — POSIX, sourced by both
5 # zsh and bash. Thin convenience layer over the same primitive workmux
6 # uses (`tmux set-option -w '@<name>_status' '<glyph>'`), so any script /
7 # hook / cron job / build watcher can tag its tmux window without
8 # pulling in workmux.

10 # Why a shared layer (not in 38_workmux.zsh): these helpers don't need
11 # any zsh feature, and the most common consumers (build scripts, deploy
12 # hooks, CI wrappers) tend to be `#!/bin/bash` or `#!/bin/sh`. Putting
13 # them in dot_config/shell/ means they Just Work from any shell.
14 #
15 # Companion: docs/tools/workmux.md → "Reusing the per-window status
16 # mechanism (without workmux)" for design rationale, the lifecycle hard
17 # rules, and the build-watcher worked example.
18 #
19 # Quick reference:
20 #
21 #   tmux_status_set my_build 🔨           # tag current window
22 #   tmux_status_set my_build 🔨 mysess:3  # tag specific window
23 #   tmux_status_get my_build              # read current window
24 #   tmux_status_clear my_build            # unset (current window)
25 #   tmux_status_clear my_build mysess:3   # unset specific window
26 #   tmux_status_clear_all my_build        # unset across every session
27 #   tmux_status_list                      # list every @*_status user-var
28 #   tmux_status_run my_build 🔨 ✅ ❌ -- npm run build
29 #                                         # set 🔨, run cmd, set ✅/❌
30 #                                         # by exit code, auto-clear on
31 #                                         # signal trap
32 #
33 # Naming convention: pass the LOGICAL name without `@` or `_status`
34 # suffix — these helpers add the `@<name>_status` wrapper. So
35 # `tmux_status_set my_build 🔨` writes `@my_build_status`. This keeps
36 # the user-var namespace tidy (`@<tool>_status` everywhere) and lets
37 # you grep for "every status producer" with `tmux_status_list`.
38 
39 # Skip silently if tmux isn't on PATH (cron, headless SSH, fresh box
40 # pre-ansible). Producers can call these unconditionally.
41 command -v tmux >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
42 
43 # Internal: validate name (alphanumeric + underscore + dash, no `@` /
44 # `_status` since we add them). Returns 0 if valid, 1 if not (with
45 # stderr diagnostic). Empty name is rejected. Names starting with
46 # `workmux` are reserved to avoid clobbering workmux's own user-var.
47 _tmux_status_validate_name() {
48     if [ -z "${1:-}" ]; then
49         printf 'tmux_status: name argument is required\n' >&2
50         return 1

53         workmux*)

58         *[!A-Za-z0-9_-]*)
59             printf 'tmux_status: name "%s" must be [A-Za-z0-9_-]+\n' "$1" >&2
60             return 1
61             ;;
62     esac
63     return 0
64 }

68 tmux_status_set() {
69     _tmux_status_validate_name "${1:-}" || return 1
70     if [ $# -lt 2 ]; then
71         printf 'tmux_status_set: usage: tmux_status_set <name> <glyph> [target]\n' >&2

91         tmux show-options -wv -t "$_target" "@${_name}_status" 2>/dev/null
92     else
93         tmux show-options -wv "@${_name}_status" 2>/dev/null
94     fi
95 }
96 
97 # tmux_status_clear <name> [target]
98 tmux_status_clear() {
99     _tmux_status_validate_name "${1:-}" || return 1
100     _name="$1"
101     _target="${2:-}"
102     if [ -n "$_target" ]; then
103         tmux set-option -w -t "$_target" -u "@${_name}_status" 2>/dev/null
104     else
105         tmux set-option -w -u "@${_name}_status" 2>/dev/null
106     fi
107 }
108 
109 # tmux_status_clear_all <name>
110 #   walk every window in every session, unset @<name>_status
111 tmux_status_clear_all() {
112     _tmux_status_validate_name "${1:-}" || return 1
113     _name="$1"
114     tmux list-windows -aF '#{session_name}:#{window_index}' 2>/dev/null | while IFS= read -r _w; do
115         tmux set-option -w -t "$_w" -u "@${_name}_status" 2>/dev/null
116     done
117 }
118 
119 # tmux_status_list
120 #   show every @*_status user-var across every window (read-only audit)
121 tmux_status_list() {
122     tmux list-windows -aF '#{session_name}:#{window_index} #{window_name}' 2>/dev/null | while IFS= read -r _line; do
123         _w="${_line%% *}"
124         # Pull every option starting with @ on this window, filter to *_status
125         tmux show-options -w -t "$_w" 2>/dev/null \
126             | awk -v w="$_line" '/^@[A-Za-z0-9_-]+_status / {print w "  " $0}'
127     done
128 }
129 
130 # tmux_status_run <name> <working_glyph> <ok_glyph> <fail_glyph> -- <cmd> [args...]
131 #   Run a command, badge the window with `working_glyph` while it runs,
132 #   then `ok_glyph` on success or `fail_glyph` on failure. Traps INT /
133 #   TERM / HUP to clear the badge instead of leaking on Ctrl+C.
134 #
135 #   Example:
136 #     tmux_status_run my_build 🔨 ✅ ❌ -- npm run build
137 #     tmux_status_run deploy   🚀 🟢 🔴 -- ./deploy.sh prod
138 tmux_status_run() {
139     _tmux_status_validate_name "${1:-}" || return 1
140     if [ $# -lt 6 ]; then
141         printf 'tmux_status_run: usage: tmux_status_run <name> <working> <ok> <fail> -- <cmd> [args...]\n' >&2
142         return 1
143     fi
144     _name="$1"
145     _working="$2"
146     _ok="$3"
147     _fail="$4"
148     shift 4
149     if [ "${1:-}" != "--" ]; then
150         # shellcheck disable=SC2016 # Backticks are literal in the diagnostic message.
151         printf 'tmux_status_run: missing `--` separator before command\n' >&2
152         return 1
153     fi
154     shift
155     if [ $# -eq 0 ]; then
156         # shellcheck disable=SC2016 # Backticks are literal in the diagnostic message.
157         printf 'tmux_status_run: no command after `--`\n' >&2
158         return 1
159     fi
160 
161     # Capture target ONCE up front — if `cmd` happens to switch tmux
162     # window, we still want the badge to land on the window the user
163     # invoked from.
164     _target=$(tmux display -p '#{session_name}:#{window_index}' 2>/dev/null)
165     [ -z "$_target" ] && _target=""
166 
167     # Trap so Ctrl+C / kill doesn't leak the working glyph forever.
168     # Use a trap that clears, then re-raises the signal default for
169     # correct exit semantics.
170     trap '_tmux_status_run_trap "$_name" "$_target"' INT TERM HUP
171 
172     tmux_status_set "$_name" "$_working" "$_target"
173     "$@"
174     _rc=$?
175     if [ $_rc -eq 0 ]; then
176         tmux_status_set "$_name" "$_ok" "$_target"
177     else
178         tmux_status_set "$_name" "$_fail" "$_target"
179     fi
180 
181     trap - INT TERM HUP
182     return $_rc
183 }
184 
185 # Internal: trap helper for tmux_status_run. Clears the badge then
186 # re-raises the signal so the calling shell sees correct $? / exit code.
187 _tmux_status_run_trap() {
188     tmux_status_clear "$1" "$2" 2>/dev/null
189     trap - INT TERM HUP
190     # Re-raise INT (most common case); for TERM/HUP we just let the
191     # shell continue — calling scripts can decide what to do via $?.
192     kill -INT $$ 2>/dev/null
193 }

1 # tmux + OSC 133 capture helpers — shell-level counterparts of the
2 # prefix + M-y / M-i tmux bindings, with an N-back index.
3 #
4 #   cpcmd [N]    last (or Nth-latest) command's INPUT  (zsh history; universal)
5 #   cpout [N]    last (or Nth-latest) command's OUTPUT (tmux copy-mode chain)
6 #   cpblock [N]  last (or Nth-latest) command's FULL BLOCK, Warp-style
7 #
8 # N defaults to 1 (= latest). N=2 is the one before that, and so on.
9 #
10 # Each prints captured text to stdout (pipe-friendly: `cpout | grep ERROR`)
11 # AND copies to system clipboard. Diagnostic + byte count go to stderr so
12 # stdout stays clean for pipes.
13 #
14 # WHY cpout/cpblock need tmux:
15 # tmux consumes OSC 133 marker bytes and only stores them as per-line
16 # attributes in its grid — `tmux capture-pane -pe` does NOT re-emit them.
17 # Outside tmux there's no portable way to recover boundaries of a past
18 # command's output (terminals like iTerm2/Ghostty have proprietary APIs,
19 # but nothing cross-terminal). cpcmd uses zsh shell history instead, so it
20 # works universally.
21 #
22 # Requires: zsh; plus tmux for cpout/cpblock.
23 
24 # Pipe stdin to system clipboard, preferring tmux's OSC 52 bridge (SSH-safe)
25 # and falling back to platform-native clipboard tools.
26 _cpx_to_clipboard() {
27   if [[ -n "$TMUX" ]]; then
28     tmux load-buffer -w -
29   elif command -v pbcopy &>/dev/null; then
30     pbcopy
31   elif command -v wl-copy &>/dev/null; then
32     wl-copy
33   elif command -v xclip &>/dev/null; then
34     xclip -selection clipboard -in
35   elif command -v xsel &>/dev/null; then
36     xsel --clipboard --input
37   else
38     cat >/dev/null
39     return 1
40   fi
41 }
42 
43 # Validate a positive-integer argument. Echoes the value on success; prints
44 # a usage hint to stderr and returns 1 on invalid input.
45 _cpx_parse_n() {
46   local name=$1 n=${2:-1}
47   if [[ ! "$n" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || (( n < 1 )); then
48     print -u2 "$name: N must be a positive integer (got: $n). Usage: $name [N]"
49     return 1
50   fi
51   print -r -- "$n"
52 }
53 
54 # Run a tmux copy-mode selection chain on the current pane. Prints selection
55 # to stdout, diagnostic (name + byte count) to stderr. Returns 1 on empty.
56 #
57 #   _cpx_tmux_select <display-name> <prev-count> <prev-cmd> [prev-args...]
58 #
59 # Chain: copy-mode → (<prev-cmd> <prev-args...>) × <prev-count> →
60 #        begin-selection → next-prompt →
61 #        copy-pipe-and-cancel "tee <tmp> | tmux load-buffer -w -" → wait-for
62 #
63 # <prev-count> is how many times to repeat the `previous-*` command before
64 # starting the selection — that's how N-back lookback is done.
65 #
66 # Depends on 02_shell_integration.zsh skipping the OSC 133 C marker for
67 # these helpers' own invocation (see the case statement there). Without
68 # that skip, `previous-prompt -o` would land on this command's own output
69 # start and the selection would be empty.
70 _cpx_tmux_select() {
71   local name=$1; shift
72   local prev_count=$1; shift
73   local tmp sentinel i _y
74   tmp="${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/cpx-$$-$RANDOM"
75   sentinel="cpx-$$-$RANDOM"
76   : > "$tmp"
77   tmux copy-mode -t "$TMUX_PANE" 2>/dev/null || return 1
78   # Seek to history bottom so N-back math is measured from a known origin.
79   tmux send-keys -t "$TMUX_PANE" -X history-bottom 2>/dev/null
80   # Sync barrier between `send-keys -X` calls: an assignment from
81   # `$(tmux display-message -p …)` is what actually forces the tmux server
82   # to commit the previous copy-mode command before it answers. Without
83   # this round-trip, bursts of `previous-prompt` calls collapse to a single
84   # cursor jump on tmux 3.6a — `sleep`, `: "$(…)"`, and bare redirection
85   # (`>/dev/null`) are ALL insufficient. The variable read is what makes zsh
86   # wait for subprocess output, which in turn serialises tmux's queue.
87   for (( i = 0; i < prev_count; i++ )); do
88     tmux send-keys -t "$TMUX_PANE" -X "$@" 2>/dev/null
89     _y=$(tmux display-message -p -t "$TMUX_PANE" '#{copy_cursor_y}' 2>/dev/null)
90   done
91   tmux send-keys -t "$TMUX_PANE" -X begin-selection 2>/dev/null
92   tmux send-keys -t "$TMUX_PANE" -X next-prompt 2>/dev/null
93   _y=$(tmux display-message -p -t "$TMUX_PANE" '#{copy_cursor_y}' 2>/dev/null)
94   tmux send-keys -t "$TMUX_PANE" -X copy-pipe-and-cancel \
95     "tee $tmp | tmux load-buffer -w - ; tmux wait-for -S $sentinel" 2>/dev/null
96   tmux wait-for "$sentinel" 2>/dev/null
97   if [[ -s "$tmp" ]]; then
98     cat "$tmp"
99     local bytes
100     bytes=$(wc -c <"$tmp" | tr -d ' ')
101     rm -f "$tmp"
102     print -u2 "$name: $bytes bytes copied to clipboard"
103     return 0
104   fi
105   rm -f "$tmp"
106   return 1
107 }
108 
109 # cpcmd [N] — last (or Nth-latest) command's INPUT. Universal: reads zsh
110 # shell history. Clean output (no prompt chrome, no terminal-echo artefacts).
111 cpcmd() {
112   emulate -L zsh
113   local n
114   n=$(_cpx_parse_n cpcmd "${1:-1}") || return 1
115   local cmd
116   # fc -ln -N -N: list entries from (-N) to (-N), inclusive — just the Nth back
117   cmd=$(fc -ln -"$n" -"$n" 2>/dev/null)
118   cmd="${cmd# }"   # strip fc's leading tab
119   cmd="${cmd# }"
120   if [[ -z "$cmd" ]]; then
121     print -u2 "cpcmd: no command at N=$n in shell history"
122     return 1
123   fi
124   printf '%s\n' "$cmd" | _cpx_to_clipboard || {
125     print -u2 "cpcmd: no clipboard tool available (install pbcopy / xclip / xsel / wl-copy, or run inside tmux)"
126     return 1
127   }
128   printf '%s\n' "$cmd"
129   print -u2 "cpcmd: ${#cmd} bytes (zsh history -$n) copied to clipboard"
130 }
131 
132 # cpout [N] — last (or Nth-latest) command's OUTPUT via tmux's OSC 133 line
133 # attrs. cpout/cpcmd/cpblock themselves are preexec-skipped for C, so N=1
134 # lands on the *previous* command's output start, N=2 on the one before, etc.
135 cpout() {
136   emulate -L zsh
137   if [[ -z "$TMUX" ]]; then
138     print -u2 "cpout: requires tmux (OSC 133 boundaries are stored per-pane by tmux). Use cpcmd for input, or your terminal's native 'copy output' if available."
139     return 1
140   fi
141   local n
142   n=$(_cpx_parse_n cpout "${1:-1}") || return 1
143   _cpx_tmux_select "cpout -$n" "$n" previous-prompt -o || {
144     print -u2 "cpout: empty at N=$n — (a) shell pre-dates chezmoi apply, run 'exec zsh' (verify: echo \$precmd_functions | grep osc133); (b) N exceeds command history in this pane; (c) target command is an alt-screen TUI (vim, htop) with no OSC 133 output."
145     return 1
146   }
147 }
148 
149 # cpblock [N] — last (or Nth-latest) command's FULL BLOCK (prompt + input +
150 # output), Warp-style. The OSC 133 A marker is embedded in PROMPT itself
151 # (02_shell_integration.zsh) so cpblock's OWN prompt carries an A too —
152 # call previous-prompt N+1 times to skip self + land N-back.
153 cpblock() {
154   emulate -L zsh
155   if [[ -z "$TMUX" ]]; then
156     print -u2 "cpblock: requires tmux (see cpout for why)."
157     return 1
158   fi
159   local n
160   n=$(_cpx_parse_n cpblock "${1:-1}") || return 1
161   _cpx_tmux_select "cpblock -$n" $(( n + 1 )) previous-prompt || {
162     print -u2 "cpblock: empty at N=$n — run 'exec zsh' if the shell pre-dates chezmoi apply, or N exceeds command history in this pane."
163     return 1
164   }
165 }
166

<tool-use data-tool-type="generic" data-tool-name="AskUserQuestion"><details>

**What UX shape do you want for the summary command?**

Options:

- **Inline print + fzf picker** - `tsum` prints a one-line summary per session to stdout; `tsum -i` opens an fzf picker (session list with summaries as preview), Enter switches client. Mirrors how `cpout`/`workmux` already work — most flexible.
- **Tmux popup + menu entry** - Add an entry to the prefix+Space popup menu (Agents submenu or top) — opens a popup with session summaries, Enter switches. No shell function; pure tmux-side.
- **Both (shell fn + popup)** - Implement the shell function first, then wire a thin tmux popup that calls it. More code surface but maximum convenience and a single source of truth for the logic.

**Which LLM CLI should drive the summary?**

Options:

- **claude -p (configurable)** - Default to `claude -p` (non-interactive Claude Code mode); fall back to `codex exec` / `gemini` via `$TSUM_BACKEND` env var. One backend works on every chezmoi-managed box.
- **codex exec** - Default to `codex exec` (already used in this repo's shell helpers). Smaller surface, but tied to one tool.
- **gemini -p** - Default to `gemini -p`. Cheapest if you use Gemini heavily, but less ubiquitous in this repo's existing patterns.

**How much context per session should be sent to the LLM?**

Options:

- **Metadata only (recommended)** - For each window: index, name, cwd, current command, pane count. Fast, ~50 lines/session, no secrets risk. Usually enough to summarize "what is this session".
- **Metadata + last 20 lines of active pane** - Adds `tmux capture-pane -p -S -20` for the active pane in each window. Richer context (live error messages, current task) but slower, risks leaking secrets to the LLM, and inflates tokens 10–50×.
- **Metadata + opt-in --deep flag** - Default to metadata only; `tsum --deep` (or `-d`) opts into the pane-capture mode for that one invocation. Best of both, slightly more code.

**Should results be cached, and for how long?**

Options:

- **Cache 10 min in $XDG_CACHE_HOME** - Store the summary JSON keyed by a hash of (session-name, window-count, last-active-time) for 10 minutes. Skips LLM call when nothing changed. `tsum -r` forces refresh.
- **No caching** - Re-run the LLM every time. Simplest implementation, but every `tsum` invocation costs an API call (~5–10s, a few cents).
- **Per-session lazy cache** - Cache each session's summary independently, invalidating only when that session's window count or layout signature changes. Most efficient but more code.

1 # AI-powered review of past commands — pipes the Nth block to a coding-agent

3 # Depends on 03_tmux_capture.zsh for `cpblock`.

6 #   aiexplain [N] [-a AGENT] [-p PROMPT] [--raw] [--no-meta]

8 #
9 # Agent auto-detection order: claude → opencode → codex → cursor-agent.
10 # Override via -a AGENT (per-call) or AICAP_AGENT env var (per-shell).
11 # Advisory-only by design; there is no --execute flag.
12 # For a back-and-forth interactive session, use `aiblock` → "Spawn agent".
13 #
14 # A fifth agent type `http` talks an OpenAI-compatible chat-completions endpoint
15 # directly via curl + jq. Use it for OpenRouter free models or local Ollama
16 # without depending on any agent CLI being installed:
17 #
18 #   AICAP_AGENT=http aifix              # OpenRouter (free Gemini Flash by default)
19 #   AICAP_AGENT=http \
20 #     AICAP_HTTP_URL=http://localhost:11434/v1/chat/completions \
21 #     AICAP_HTTP_MODEL=qwen2.5-coder:7b aifix
22 #
23 # `http` is opt-in: it is never auto-detected (nothing on PATH to probe).
24 #
25 # Env-var defaults (set in ~/.zshrc or a 99_local_*.zsh to override):
26 #
27 #   AICAP_AGENT            default: (unset — auto-detect)
28 #                                        force a specific agent: claude | opencode |
29 #                                        codex | cursor-agent | http
30 #   AICAP_CLAUDE_MODEL     default: haiku           (claude --model alias)
31 #   AICAP_OPENCODE_MODEL   default: github-copilot/claude-haiku-4.5
32 #   AICAP_CODEX_MODEL      default: gpt-5-mini
33 #   AICAP_CURSOR_MODEL     default: (unset — let cursor-agent pick)

55 : "${AICAP_PRETTIFY:=1}"

58 _aiagent_autodetect() {
59   local cand
60   for cand in claude opencode codex cursor-agent; do
61     if command -v "$cand" &>/dev/null; then
62       print -r -- "$cand"
63       return 0
64     fi
65   done
66   return 1
67 }
68 
69 # Background spinner on stderr while the agent is thinking. Skipped when
70 # AICAP_SPINNER=0 or stderr isn't a tty (so pipes / file redirects stay
71 # clean). The spinner subprocess is disowned via `&!` so it survives the
72 # command substitution that invokes the agent.
73 _AICAP_SPIN_PID=
74 _aicap_spinner_start() {
75   [[ "$AICAP_SPINNER" != "1" ]] && return 0
76   [[ ! -t 2 ]] && return 0
77   local label=${1:-thinking}
78   (
79     trap 'exit 0' TERM INT HUP
80     local frames=('⠋' '⠙' '⠹' '⠸' '⠼' '⠴' '⠦' '⠧' '⠇' '⠏')
81     local i=0
82     while true; do
83       printf '\r\e[K%s %s' "${frames[$(( (i % 10) + 1 ))]}" "$label" >&2
84       (( i++ ))
85       sleep 0.1
86     done
87   ) &!
88   _AICAP_SPIN_PID=$!
89 }
90 
91 _aicap_spinner_stop() {
92   [[ -z "$_AICAP_SPIN_PID" ]] && return 0
93   kill "$_AICAP_SPIN_PID" 2>/dev/null
94   # Drain; zsh waits on PIDs even if disowned as long as we know the PID.
95   wait "$_AICAP_SPIN_PID" 2>/dev/null
96   _AICAP_SPIN_PID=
97   [[ -t 2 ]] && printf '\r\e[K' >&2
98 }
99 
100 # Pretty-print stdin as Markdown: glow > bat > raw. Skips prettify if stdout
101 # is NOT a tty (so pipes stay clean) or AICAP_PRETTIFY=0.
102 _aicap_prettify() {
103   if [[ "$AICAP_PRETTIFY" != "1" ]] || [[ ! -t 1 ]]; then
104     cat
105   elif command -v glow &>/dev/null; then
106     glow -
107   elif command -v bat &>/dev/null; then
108     bat --language=md --style=plain --paging=never --color=always
109   else
110     cat

# Plan: `tsum` — AI-powered tmux session summarizer

## Context

User routinely has 10+ tmux sessions open with cryptic names (`9`, `10`, `19`,
`20`, `tries/2026-03-23-RL-Investigation`, `coding-agent/…`). Glancing at
`tmux ls` no longer tells them what each session is *for* or which windows are
load-bearing. The user wants a single command that asks an LLM to summarize
every session ("what is this session", "which 1-3 windows are important"),
shown both as plain stdout (`tsum`) and as a tmux popup picker that switches
clients on Enter.

Outcome: one new command `tsum` + one new tmux menu entry, reusing the repo's
existing agent autodetect order (claude → opencode → codex → cursor-agent) and
caching results for 10 min in `$XDG_CACHE_HOME` so the LLM cost stays bounded.

## Architecture

Three layers, one per managed file:

\```
┌── ~/.config/tmux/tmux-session-summary.py    ── core: capture + LLM + cache
├── ~/.config/shell/61_tmux_summary.sh        ── thin POSIX wrapper `tsum`
└── ~/.config/tmux/executable_menu-session.sh ── menu row → popup → fzf
\```

Core in Python because the repo already has `scripts/aiblock.py` as the
template for PEP 723 / `uv run --script` agent invokers — caching JSON,
parsing `tmux list-windows -F`, building structured prompts, and fzf piping
are all cleaner in Python than POSIX sh. Wrapper is POSIX (in `dot_config/shell/`)
so bash users get `tsum` too — the function does nothing zsh-specific.

## Files to add / modify

### 1. New: `dot_config/tmux/executable_tmux-session-summary.py`

PEP 723 inline-deps script (`#!/usr/bin/env -S uv run --script`, deps:
`rich>=13.9`). Modeled directly on
[`scripts/aiblock.py`](../../scripts/aiblock.py) — reuse the
`AGENT_CONFIG` dict + `AICAP_*` env-var defaults verbatim (see
`scripts/aiblock.py:55-78`) so a user's existing `AICAP_AGENT` /
`AICAP_CLAUDE_MODEL` overrides apply transparently.

Subcommands (CLI surface):

\```
tmux-session-summary.py list       [--deep] [--refresh] [--dry-run]
tmux-session-summary.py picker     [--deep] [--refresh]
\```

Behaviour:

- **`list`** — print one block per session to stdout. Plain text, switch-friendly:
  \```
  9    [12w] dotfiles edits — agent contract refactor
         └ w7: nvim CLAUDE.md   (primary editor)
         └ w2: chezmoi apply test runner
  10   [10w] ML scraper — currently running
         └ w3: python scrape.py (5h uptime, active)
  \```
- **`picker`** — print TSV `<session>\t<one-line-summary>` to stdout for fzf
  consumption.
- **`--deep`** — additionally include `tmux capture-pane -p -S -20 -t <sess>:<win>`
  output for each window's active pane in the LLM prompt. Off by default;
  inflates tokens 10–50× and risks leaking pane contents.
- **`--refresh` / `-r`** — bypass cache, force a fresh LLM call.
- **`--dry-run`** — print the prompt that *would* be sent to the LLM without
  invoking; lets the user see what context is leaked before trusting it.

Capture pipeline (per CLAUDE.md "Tmux Content Capture Patterns"):

1. `tmux list-sessions -F '#{session_name}|#{session_windows}|#{session_created}|#{session_attached}|#{session_last_attached}'`
2. For each session: `tmux list-windows -t <s> -F '#{window_index}|#{window_name}|#{window_active}|#{pane_current_path}|#{pane_current_command}|#{window_panes}'`
3. (`--deep` only) `tmux capture-pane -p -S -20 -t <s>:<active_win>` once per session

Caching:

- Path: `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/tmux-session-summary/<hostname>-<sig>.json`
  (falls back to `~/.cache/tmux-session-summary/` if `XDG_CACHE_HOME` unset).
- Signature: SHA-256 over the sorted `tmux list-sessions` + `list-windows`
  output (so adding a window invalidates; idle navigation doesn't).
- TTL: 10 min from `generated_at` ISO-8601 stamp.
- Cache contains one record per session keyed by `session_name`; if a session
  vanishes between runs it's just dropped.
- `tsum -r` writes a fresh entry, replacing whatever existed.

Agent invocation:

- Reuse `AGENT_CONFIG` from `scripts/aiblock.py:72-78` (claude / opencode /
  codex / cursor-agent / http). Autodetect order matches
  `dot_config/zsh/tools/04_ai_capture.zsh:58-67`. Pin model defaults to the
  cheap tier already chosen in that file (`haiku`, `gpt-5-mini`, etc.) — these
  are summarization tasks, no need for frontier models.
- One LLM call per `tsum` invocation, not per session: send all sessions in
  one structured prompt, ask for a JSON array of `{session, summary,
  important_windows[]}` back. JSON output is parsed; on parse failure fall
  back to raw text rendering.
- Use the same `_aicap_spinner_start/stop` pattern from
  `dot_config/zsh/tools/04_ai_capture.zsh:74-98` (re-implemented in Python
  with `rich.status.Status` or a small braille spinner on stderr).

Failure modes:

- No agent CLI on PATH → exit 1 with the same message style as
  `04_ai_capture.zsh:328` (mentions all four candidates by name).
- Not inside tmux **and** no `--list-from-pty` flag → exit 1 with hint.
- LLM call times out (>60s) → fall back to printing the raw metadata
  capture without summaries (degraded mode beats no output).

### 2. New: `dot_config/shell/61_tmux_summary.sh`

POSIX-shared shell wrapper, sourced by both `~/.zshrc` and `~/.bashrc`
(slot 61 sits right after `60_tmux_status.sh` which it complements).

\```sh
# Skip silently if tmux not on PATH (cron, headless boxes pre-ansible).
command -v tmux >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0

tsum() {
    # Flags: -d|--deep, -r|--refresh, -i|--interactive (fzf picker), --dry-run
    # Default: print plain-text summary list
    # -i: pipe `picker` mode to fzf, on Enter call `tmux switch-client -t {1}`
    # All other flags forwarded to ~/.config/tmux/tmux-session-summary.py
    …
}
\```

Notes:

- ~40 lines total; argparse loop + one of two invocation paths (plain `list`
  or `picker | fzf …`).
- Does NOT depend on `_aiagent_autodetect` from `04_ai_capture.zsh` (zsh-only)
  — early-return uses a tiny POSIX probe: `for c in claude opencode codex
  cursor-agent; do command -v "$c" >/dev/null && break; done` or skip the
  probe entirely and let the Python script emit the canonical error.
- `-i` requires `fzf` on PATH; otherwise prints a hint and falls back to plain
  list.

### 3. Modify: `dot_config/tmux/executable_menu-session.sh`

Add one row inside the existing `rows=( … )` array (this submenu is the right
home: the feature is *about understanding sessions*; LLM is just the
implementation). Conditional on `~/.config/tmux/tmux-session-summary.py`
existing so the row hides on hosts that haven't done `chezmoi apply` yet:

\```bash
if [ -x "$HOME/.config/tmux/tmux-session-summary.py" ]; then
  rows+=(
    "AI session summary"  u  "display-popup -E -w 90% -h 70% -d '#{pane_current_path}' -T ' AI session summary ' '$HOME/.config/tmux/tmux-session-summary.py picker | fzf --delimiter=\"\\t\" --with-nth=2 --preview \"echo {2}\" --bind \"enter:execute-silent(tmux switch-client -t {1})+abort\"'"
  )
fi
\```

Hard rule check (CLAUDE.md "Tmux Popup Menu"):

- Popup at 90%×70% — the inner fzf paginates so the menu-too-tall failure
  doesn't apply to fzf content.
- The outer `display-menu` row count: this submenu currently has ~8 rows; one
  more is safe well under the 14-row cap. Verify by running
  `prefix+Space → Sessions` after install.
- The fzf invocation has braces and pipes — they live inside the *executed
  shell command* not the tmux `display-menu` parser, so the parser-quoting
  trap doesn't apply.

### 4. Modify: `docs/shells/aliases.md`

Add one row to the function table (header at `docs/shells/aliases.md:38-39`):

\```markdown
| `tsum` | function | `dot_config/shell/61_tmux_summary.sh` | AI-summarize tmux sessions (claude/opencode/codex/cursor-agent fallback; cached 10 min; `-d` deep, `-i` fzf-pick & switch). |
\```

### 5. Optional: `docs/tools/tmux/session-summary.md` + `mkdocs.yml` nav

Short reference page (~80 lines) covering: invocation forms, env vars
(`AICAP_*`, `TSUM_CACHE_TTL`), what gets sent to the LLM (so users can audit
before opting in), deep-mode warning, cache invalidation rules. **Defer
unless the user wants it** — `aliases.md` row + inline header docstring in
the Python script may be enough.

If added: append a nav entry under `Tools → Tmux` in `mkdocs.yml`, then
`uv run mkdocs build --strict`.

## Reused utilities (do not reinvent)

| Need | Reuse from | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Agent CLI fallback order | `dot_config/zsh/tools/04_ai_capture.zsh:58-67` | Same order the user already expects (`_aiagent_autodetect`) — inlined as a Python equivalent in the new script. |
| Per-agent invocation flags / env defaults | `scripts/aiblock.py:55-78` (`AGENT_CONFIG`, `AICAP_*`) | Already proven; using identical env vars means user's `AICAP_CLAUDE_MODEL=haiku` etc. carry over automatically. |
| Spinner on stderr while LLM is thinking | `dot_config/zsh/tools/04_ai_capture.zsh:74-98` (`_aicap_spinner_start/stop`) | Reimplement small Python equivalent — non-tty/AICAP_SPINNER=0 must remain a no-op. |
| Tmux metadata capture format | `dot_config/shell/60_tmux_status.sh:114` (`tmux list-windows -aF '…'`) and `dot_config/zsh/tools/38_workmux.zsh:39` | Same format strings; consistent across helpers. |
| Pane content capture | `dot_config/zsh/tools/03_tmux_capture.zsh` (`tmux capture-pane -p …`) | Same flag set; `--deep` mode mirrors `cpout`'s scope (just last N lines, no copy-mode chain needed since we don't need OSC 133 boundaries). |
| Popup script convention | `dot_config/tmux/executable_menu-agents.sh:11` (`display-popup -E -w 80% -h 70% -d '#{pane_current_path}' -T ' Title '`) | Same template; just swap the inner command. |

## Cross-file maintenance touchpoints (per CLAUDE.md)

- **Alias/shell function** → add row to `docs/shells/aliases.md` ✓ (covered in §4 above).
- **Three-tier file placement** → core script under `dot_config/tmux/`,
  wrapper in `dot_config/shell/` (POSIX shared) — both shells get `tsum`. No
  zsh-only widgets needed. ✓
- **Keybinding cross-check** → no new `Ctrl+`/`Alt+` binding (menu-entry only,
  reached via `prefix+Space → Sessions`). ✓
- **`docs/**/*.md` nav** → only triggers if §5 (the optional doc page) is
  added. Defer until the user asks. ✓
- **chezmoi-templating** → none of the new files need `{{ … }}` predicates;
  they Just Work on macOS / Linux alike. The Python shebang `#!/usr/bin/env
  -S uv run --script` is the same pattern as `scripts/aiblock.py`. ✓

## Verification (run after implementation)

1. `chezmoi apply` (then `source ~/.zshrc` or `exec zsh`) — confirms the new
   files land and `tsum` is on PATH.
2. `tsum --dry-run` — prints the prompt that would be sent (audit what's
   leaked to the LLM; no API call).
3. `tsum` on the user's current host (12 sessions visible in the snapshot):
   confirm one-block-per-session output, plausible summaries.
4. `tsum` again immediately → cache hit, returns in <500 ms with no spinner.
5. `tsum -r` → cache bypass, fresh LLM call.
6. `tsum -d` → output includes pane-content-informed details (e.g. picks up
   on a long-running `python scrape.py`).
7. `tsum -i` → fzf opens with summaries, Enter switches client to the chosen

8. `prefix+Space → Sessions → AI session summary` → tmux popup opens, fzf
   inside, Enter switches the underlying client. **Resize terminal vertically

9. `AICAP_AGENT=opencode tsum -r` → verifies the fallback chain honours the

10. Unset every agent CLI from PATH (`PATH=/usr/bin tsum`) → exits 1 with the
    "install one of claude/opencode/codex/cursor-agent" message.
11. `mkdocs build --strict` if §5 doc page added; otherwise skip.

## Out of scope (intentionally)

- Per-session lazy caching (user picked the simpler 10-min-blanket strategy).
- A standalone Python TUI like `aiblock` — `tsum -i` via fzf is leaner.
- Auto-renaming sessions based on the summary (destructive; ask later).
- Multi-host summary (this is local-host only; fleet-status already exists).
- Putting the menu row under `executable_menu-agents.sh` instead of
  `executable_menu-session.sh` — the feature is *about sessions*, AI is the
  implementation detail.

# Plan: `tsum` — AI-powered tmux session summarizer

## Context

User routinely has 10+ tmux sessions open with cryptic names (`9`, `10`, `19`,
`20`, `tries/2026-03-23-RL-Investigation`, `coding-agent/…`). Glancing at
`tmux ls` no longer tells them what each session is *for* or which windows are
load-bearing. The user wants a single command that asks an LLM to summarize
every session ("what is this session", "which 1-3 windows are important"),
shown both as plain stdout (`tsum`) and as a tmux popup picker that switches
clients on Enter.

Outcome: one new command `tsum` + one new tmux menu entry, reusing the repo's
existing agent autodetect order (claude → opencode → codex → cursor-agent) and
caching results for 10 min in `$XDG_CACHE_HOME` so the LLM cost stays bounded.

## Architecture

Three layers, one per managed file:

```

┌── ~/.config/tmux/tmux-session-summary.py    ── core: capture + LLM + cache
├── ~/.config/shell/61_tmux_summary.sh        ── thin POSIX wrapper `tsum`
└── ~/.config/tmux/executable_menu-session.sh ── menu row → popup → fzf

```

Core in Python because the repo already has `scripts/aiblock.py` as the
template for PEP 723 / `uv run --script` agent invokers — caching JSON,
parsing `tmux list-windows -F`, building structured prompts, and fzf piping
are all cleaner in Python than POSIX sh. Wrapper is POSIX (in `dot_config/shell/`)
so bash users get `tsum` too — the function does nothing zsh-specific.

## Files to add / modify

### 1. New: `dot_config/tmux/executable_tmux-session-summary.py`

PEP 723 inline-deps script (`#!/usr/bin/env -S uv run --script`, deps:
`rich>=13.9`). Modeled directly on
[`scripts/aiblock.py`](../../scripts/aiblock.py) — reuse the
`AGENT_CONFIG` dict + `AICAP_*` env-var defaults verbatim (see
`scripts/aiblock.py:55-78`) so a user's existing `AICAP_AGENT` /
`AICAP_CLAUDE_MODEL` overrides apply transparently.

Subcommands (CLI surface):

```

tmux-session-summary.py list       [--deep] [--refresh] [--dry-run]
tmux-session-summary.py picker     [--deep] [--refresh]

```

Behaviour:

- **`list`** — print one block per session to stdout. Plain text, switch-friendly:
  ```

  9    [12w] dotfiles edits — agent contract refactor
         └ w7: nvim CLAUDE.md   (primary editor)
         └ w2: chezmoi apply test runner
  10   [10w] ML scraper — currently running
         └ w3: python scrape.py (5h uptime, active)

  ```
- **`picker`** — print TSV `<session>\t<one-line-summary>` to stdout for fzf
  consumption.
- **`--deep`** — additionally include `tmux capture-pane -p -S -20 -t <sess>:<win>`
  output for each window's active pane in the LLM prompt. Off by default;
  inflates tokens 10–50× and risks leaking pane contents.
- **`--refresh` / `-r`** — bypass cache, force a fresh LLM call.
- **`--dry-run`** — print the prompt that *would* be sent to the LLM without
  invoking; lets the user see what context is leaked before trusting it.

Capture pipeline (per CLAUDE.md "Tmux Content Capture Patterns"):

1. `tmux list-sessions -F '#{session_name}|#{session_windows}|#{session_created}|#{session_attached}|#{session_last_attached}'`
2. For each session: `tmux list-windows -t <s> -F '#{window_index}|#{window_name}|#{window_active}|#{pane_current_path}|#{pane_current_command}|#{window_panes}'`
3. (`--deep` only) `tmux capture-pane -p -S -20 -t <s>:<active_win>` once per session

Caching:

- Path: `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/tmux-session-summary/<hostname>-<sig>.json`
  (falls back to `~/.cache/tmux-session-summary/` if `XDG_CACHE_HOME` unset).
- Signature: SHA-256 over the sorted `tmux list-sessions` + `list-windows`
  output (so adding a window invalidates; idle navigation doesn't).
- TTL: 10 min from `generated_at` ISO-8601 stamp.
- Cache contains one record per session keyed by `session_name`; if a session
  vanishes between runs it's just dropped.
- `tsum -r` writes a fresh entry, replacing whatever existed.

Agent invocation:

- Reuse `AGENT_CONFIG` from `scripts/aiblock.py:72-78` (claude / opencode /
  codex / cursor-agent / http). Autodetect order matches
  `dot_config/zsh/tools/04_ai_capture.zsh:58-67`. Pin model defaults to the
  cheap tier already chosen in that file (`haiku`, `gpt-5-mini`, etc.) — these
  are summarization tasks, no need for frontier models.
- One LLM call per `tsum` invocation, not per session: send all sessions in
  one structured prompt, ask for a JSON array of `{session, summary,
  important_windows[]}` back. JSON output is parsed; on parse failure fall
  back to raw text rendering.
- Use the same `_aicap_spinner_start/stop` pattern from
  `dot_config/zsh/tools/04_ai_capture.zsh:74-98` (re-implemented in Python
  with `rich.status.Status` or a small braille spinner on stderr).

Failure modes:

- No agent CLI on PATH → exit 1 with the same message style as
  `04_ai_capture.zsh:328` (mentions all four candidates by name).
- Not inside tmux **and** no `--list-from-pty` flag → exit 1 with hint.
- LLM call times out (>60s) → fall back to printing the raw metadata
  capture without summaries (degraded mode beats no output).

### 2. New: `dot_config/shell/61_tmux_summary.sh`

POSIX-shared shell wrapper, sourced by both `~/.zshrc` and `~/.bashrc`
(slot 61 sits right after `60_tmux_status.sh` which it complements).

```sh
# Skip silently if tmux not on PATH (cron, headless boxes pre-ansible).
command -v tmux >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0

tsum() {
    # Flags: -d|--deep, -r|--refresh, -i|--interactive (fzf picker), --dry-run
    # Default: print plain-text summary list
    # -i: pipe `picker` mode to fzf, on Enter call `tmux switch-client -t {1}`
    # All other flags forwarded to ~/.config/tmux/tmux-session-summary.py
    …
}
```

Notes:

- ~40 lines total; argparse loop + one of two invocation paths (plain `list`
  or `picker | fzf …`).
- Does NOT depend on `_aiagent_autodetect` from `04_ai_capture.zsh` (zsh-only)
  — early-return uses a tiny POSIX probe: `for c in claude opencode codex
  cursor-agent; do command -v "$c" >/dev/null && break; done` or skip the
  probe entirely and let the Python script emit the canonical error.
- `-i` requires `fzf` on PATH; otherwise prints a hint and falls back to plain
  list.

### 3. Modify: `dot_config/tmux/executable_menu-session.sh`

Add one row inside the existing `rows=( … )` array (this submenu is the right
home: the feature is _about understanding sessions_; LLM is just the
implementation). Conditional on `~/.config/tmux/tmux-session-summary.py`
existing so the row hides on hosts that haven't done `chezmoi apply` yet:

```bash
if [ -x "$HOME/.config/tmux/tmux-session-summary.py" ]; then
  rows+=(
    "AI session summary"  u  "display-popup -E -w 90% -h 70% -d '#{pane_current_path}' -T ' AI session summary ' '$HOME/.config/tmux/tmux-session-summary.py picker | fzf --delimiter=\"\\t\" --with-nth=2 --preview \"echo {2}\" --bind \"enter:execute-silent(tmux switch-client -t {1})+abort\"'"
  )
fi
```

Hard rule check (CLAUDE.md "Tmux Popup Menu"):

- Popup at 90%×70% — the inner fzf paginates so the menu-too-tall failure
  doesn't apply to fzf content.
- The outer `display-menu` row count: this submenu currently has ~8 rows; one
  more is safe well under the 14-row cap. Verify by running
  `prefix+Space → Sessions` after install.
- The fzf invocation has braces and pipes — they live inside the _executed
  shell command_ not the tmux `display-menu` parser, so the parser-quoting
  trap doesn't apply.

## Verification (run after implementation)

1. `chezmoi apply` (then `source ~/.zshrc` or `exec zsh`) — confirms the new
   files land and `tsum` is on PATH.
2. `tsum --dry-run` — prints the prompt that would be sent (audit what's
   leaked to the LLM; no API call).
3. `tsum` on the user's current host (12 sessions visible in the snapshot):
   confirm one-block-per-session output, plausible summaries.
4. `tsum` again immediately → cache hit, returns in <500 ms with no spinner.
5. `tsum -r` → cache bypass, fresh LLM call.
6. `tsum -d` → output includes pane-content-informed details (e.g. picks up
   on a long-running `python scrape.py`).
7. `tsum -i` → fzf opens with summaries, Enter switches client to the chosen
   session.
8. `prefix+Space → Sessions → AI session summary` → tmux popup opens, fzf
   inside, Enter switches the underlying client. **Resize terminal vertically
   to ~22 rows and retest** (CLAUDE.md "menu-too-tall silent failure" rule).
9. `AICAP_AGENT=opencode tsum -r` → verifies the fallback chain honours the
   override env var.
10. Unset every agent CLI from PATH (`PATH=/usr/bin tsum`) → exits 1 with the
    "install one of claude/opencode/codex/cursor-agent" message.
11. `mkdocs build --strict` if §5 doc page added; otherwise skip.

## Out of scope (intentionally)

- Per-session lazy caching (user picked the simpler 10-min-blanket strategy).
- A standalone Python TUI like `aiblock` — `tsum -i` via fzf is leaner.
- Auto-renaming sessions based on the summary (destructive; ask later).
- Multi-host summary (this is local-host only; fleet-status already exists).
- Putting the menu row under `executable_menu-agents.sh` instead of
  `executable_menu-session.sh` — the feature is _about sessions_, AI is the
  implementation detail.

89 def detect_agents() -> list[str]:
90     """Return the subset of known agents found on PATH, in preference order.
91 
92     The `http` agent has nothing to probe on PATH; it's only included when
93     AICAP_AGENT=http is explicitly set (so the user opted in via the same
94     env var the zsh wrappers honour).

96     found = [a for a in AGENT_CONFIG if a != "http" and shutil.which(a)]

102 def zsh_run(code: str, timeout: float = 5.0) -> str:
103     """Run `zsh -ic CODE` and return stdout (strip trailing newline).
104 
105     -ic is needed so our zsh config loads (sourcing 03_tmux_capture.zsh etc.).
106     """
107     # $ZDOTDIR is set by chezmoi's 00_exports; pass-through so an interactive
108     # zsh finds the user's rc. Inherits TMUX so cpblock sees the right pane.
109     result = subprocess.run(
110         ["zsh", "-ic", code],
111         capture_output=True,
112         text=True,
113         timeout=timeout,
114         env=os.environ,
115     )
116     return result.stdout.rstrip("\n")
117 
118 
119 def list_recent_commands(n: int = 20) -> list[HistoryEntry]:
120     """Return the last `n` shell commands as HistoryEntry(N, cmd).
121 
122     Reads $AIBLOCK_HIST_DUMP (written by the zsh `aiblock` wrapper via
123     `fc -ln -30`) — a `zsh -ic fc …` subshell does NOT see the current
124     shell's in-memory history, and `fc -R` from HISTFILE misses commands
125     that haven't been flushed yet. The env-passed dump is the only
126     reliable source for "what did the USER just run".
127 
128     Falls back to parsing $HISTFILE directly if the dump env var isn't
129     set (e.g. someone ran the script without the wrapper).
130 
131     Returned list is ordered most-recent-first, with `.n` matching what
132     cpblock/cpcmd/cpout expect as their positional N arg.
133     """
134     dump_path = os.environ.get("AIBLOCK_HIST_DUMP")
135     lines: list[str] = []
136     if dump_path and os.path.isfile(dump_path):
137         with open(dump_path, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") as f:
138             lines = [ln.strip() for ln in f if ln.strip()]
139     else:
140         # Fallback: parse HISTFILE directly.
141         histfile = os.environ.get("HISTFILE") or os.path.expanduser("~/.zsh_history")
142         if os.path.isfile(histfile):
143             with open(histfile, encoding="latin-1", errors="replace") as f:
144                 raw = f.readlines()
145             for raw_ln in raw[-n * 3:]:  # last 3N raw lines (covers line continuations)
146                 s = raw_ln.rstrip("\n").strip()
147                 if not s:
148                     continue
149                 # EXTENDED_HISTORY format: ": TIMESTAMP:DURATION;CMD"
150                 if s.startswith(": "):
151                     parts = s.split(";", 1)
152                     if len(parts) == 2:
153                         s = parts[1]
154                 lines.append(s)
155     # Take the last n, reverse so index 1 == most recent.
156     lines = lines[-n:]
157     return [HistoryEntry(n=i, command=cmd) for i, cmd in enumerate(reversed(lines), start=1)]
158

165 def invoke_agent_oneshot(agent: str, prompt: str) -> tuple[str, dict]:
166     """Invoke an agent in non-interactive mode; return (reply_text, metadata).
167 
168     For Claude, we request --output-format json so we can pull usage/cost
169     into the metadata dict. Other agents fall back to text output with a
170     minimal metadata dict containing just the model name.
171     """
172     base = AGENT_CONFIG[agent]["base"]
173     meta: dict = {"agent": agent, "model": _model_for(agent)}
174 
175     if agent == "http":
176         return _invoke_http_oneshot(prompt, meta)
177 
178     if agent == "claude" and AICAP_SHOW_METADATA:
179         result = subprocess.run(
180             [*base, "--output-format", "json", prompt],
181             capture_output=True,
182             text=True,
183             timeout=180.0,
184         )
185         if result.returncode != 0:
186             console.print(f"[red]{agent} exited {result.returncode}[/red]")
187             if result.stderr:
188                 console.print(f"[dim]{result.stderr}[/dim]")
189             return "", meta
190         try:
191             parsed = json.loads(result.stdout)
192             # Claude's JSON has no top-level `.model`; the actual model name
193             # lives as the single key of `.modelUsage`.
194             mu = parsed.get("modelUsage") or {}
195             if mu:
196                 meta["model"] = next(iter(mu.keys()))
197             usage = parsed.get("usage", {})
198             meta["input_tokens"] = usage.get("input_tokens")
199             meta["output_tokens"] = usage.get("output_tokens")
200             meta["cache_read"] = usage.get("cache_read_input_tokens") or 0
201             meta["cache_create"] = usage.get("cache_creation_input_tokens") or 0
202             meta["cost_usd"] = parsed.get("total_cost_usd")
203             meta["duration_ms"] = parsed.get("duration_ms")
204             return parsed.get("result", ""), meta
205         except json.JSONDecodeError:
206             return result.stdout, meta  # fall back to raw
207 
208     result = subprocess.run(
209         [*base, prompt],
210         capture_output=True,
211         text=True,
212         timeout=180.0,
213     )
214     if result.returncode != 0:
215         console.print(f"[red]{agent} exited {result.returncode}[/red]")
216         if result.stderr:
217             console.print(f"[dim]{result.stderr}[/dim]")
218     return result.stdout, meta

223         "claude": AICAP_CLAUDE_MODEL,
224         "opencode": AICAP_OPENCODE_MODEL,
225         "codex": AICAP_CODEX_MODEL,

231 def _invoke_http_oneshot(prompt: str, meta: dict) -> tuple[str, dict]:
232     """Talk an OpenAI-compatible chat-completions endpoint via urllib.
233 
234     Same code path serves OpenRouter (with Bearer key) and local Ollama
235     (no auth). Mirrors the zsh `http` branch in 04_ai_capture.zsh.
236     """
237     payload = json.dumps({
238         "model": AICAP_HTTP_MODEL,
239         "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": prompt}],
240         "stream": False,
241     }).encode("utf-8")
242     headers = {"Content-Type": "application/json"}
243     if AICAP_HTTP_API_KEY:
244         headers["Authorization"] = f"Bearer {AICAP_HTTP_API_KEY}"
245     req = urllib.request.Request(AICAP_HTTP_URL, data=payload, headers=headers, method="POST")
246     try:
247         with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=180.0) as resp:
248             body = resp.read().decode("utf-8", errors="replace")
249     except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
250         err_body = e.read().decode("utf-8", errors="replace") if e.fp else ""
251         console.print(f"[red]http: HTTP {e.code} from {AICAP_HTTP_URL}[/red]")
252         if err_body:
253             console.print(f"[dim]{err_body[:500]}[/dim]")
254         return "", meta
255     except urllib.error.URLError as e:
256         console.print(f"[red]http: connection failed: {e.reason}[/red]")
257         return "", meta
258     try:
259         parsed = json.loads(body)
260     except json.JSONDecodeError:
261         console.print(f"[red]http: non-JSON response[/red] [dim]{body[:300]}[/dim]")
262         return "", meta
263     if isinstance(parsed.get("error"), dict):
264         msg = parsed["error"].get("message", str(parsed["error"]))
265         console.print(f"[red]http: API error: {msg}[/red]")
266         return "", meta
267     try:
268         reply = parsed["choices"][0]["message"]["content"]
269     except (KeyError, IndexError, TypeError):
270         console.print(f"[red]http: unexpected response shape[/red] [dim]{body[:300]}[/dim]")
271         return "", meta
272     usage = parsed.get("usage") or {}
273     meta["input_tokens"] = usage.get("prompt_tokens")
274     meta["output_tokens"] = usage.get("completion_tokens")
275     return reply, meta

278 def format_metadata(meta: dict) -> str:
